name: Burako Argentinean
description: Burako is a Canasta-like Rummy game played in Argentina using 106 numbered tiles (similar to Rummikub tiles). Four players in partnerships meld sequences (escaleras) and sets (piernas) to create canastas (7+ tile melds). The game features muertos (extra hands) picked up by first players to empty their initial hand.
deck: 106 tiles (two each of 1-13 in four colors + 2 jokers)

history.origins: Burako is the Argentinean tile version of Buraco, which originated in South America in the 1940s. While Brazil developed Buraco with cards, Argentina adapted it to use tiles similar to those used in Rummikub and Turkish Okey.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Argentinean tile version Burako developed
Late 20th century: Gained popularity in Argentina and neighboring countries
Modern era: Available in digital format and online play
history.cultural: Burako is a popular social game in Argentina, commonly played in homes, clubs, and cafes. The tile format makes it particularly family-friendly and accessible to players who may not be familiar with standard playing cards.
history.evolution: The game evolved from the card game Buraco/Burraco family, adapting to tiles which are also used for Rummikub and Turkish Okey. The tile format makes the game more tactile and visually distinct from card versions.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite)
setup.deck: 106 tiles: two of each number 1-13 in four colors (black, blue, red, yellow) plus two jokers (comodÃ­n). Tiles are placed on racks so each player sees only their own tiles.
setup.dealing: Tiles mixed face down. Each player draws 11 tiles onto their rack. Two face-down stacks of 11 tiles (muertos) set aside. Remaining 40 tiles form stock in four piles of 10.
setup.equipment: 106 Burako tiles with racks, table space for melds

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 3000+ points by melding tiles into sequences and sets, creating canastas (7+ tile melds), and going out.
rules.gameplay: First player draws, decides to keep or discard, then may meld and discards. Other players: draw from stock or take all discards; optionally meld escaleras (same-color sequences) or piernas (same-number sets); discard one tile. First player to empty hand takes a muerto (11-tile extra hand). Team can go out after taking muerto and having at least one canasta.
keyRules: 106 tiles: two each of 1-13 in four colors + 2 jokers
Two 11-tile muertos set aside for first players out
Escalera = sequence of 3+ consecutive same-color tiles
Pierna = set of 3+ same-number tiles (any colors)
Max one wild tile (joker or 2) per meld
1 can be low (next to 2) or high (next to 13)
Need canasta and taken muerto to go out

strategy.basic: Focus on creating valid melds quickly. Use wild tiles (jokers and 2s) to complete difficult melds. Watch which tiles your partner is collecting. Take muerto when you have a strong position to use the extra tiles.
strategy.intermediate: Track which tiles have been played and discarded. Coordinate with partner on escalera vs pierna strategies. Time your go-out carefully - going out early may deny opponents their muerto bonus. Balance pure vs impure canastas.
strategy.advanced: Calculate optimal discard pile takes based on visible tiles. Force opponents into difficult positions by holding key tiles. Advanced tile counting to predict opponent hands. Optimize meld layouts for maximum scoring potential.
tips: Always try to create at least one pure canasta for going out
Save wild tiles for critical meld completions
Watch partner's discards for signals about their hand
Going out quickly can deny opponents their muerto bonus
Consider holding key tiles to block opponent escaleras
Pure canastas score double compared to impure
The 1 tile is flexible - can be high or low

scoring.description: At the end of each hand both teams total the tile values of all tiles in their melds, subtract the values of tiles left in hand, and apply bonuses and penalties for canastas, going out, and unused muertos.
scoring.winCondition: Teams accumulate scores over multiple hands; when a team reaches or exceeds 3000 points, the team with the higher total score wins the game.
